pr_title: ERR: deprecate all old ERR_load_ and stop producing new ones
pr_body:
This is done by collecting all the pre-3.0 `ERR_load_` function declarations in separate legacy header files, and re-implement them in terms of internal functions.

The way we now load all the strings in the libraries is through internal functions.

This removes the need to document generated functions that we don't use or want to publish.

Fixes #10527
pr_comments: CIs are happy, so time for a final review?

issue_context.title: New ERR_load_xxx_strings() functions should not be public
issue_context.body:
The `util/mkerr.pl` script will automatically create new `ERR_load_xxx_stinrgs()` functions where needed and make them public. This results in PRs like #10394 adding these functions to "missingcrypto.txt" to avoid having to document them - which is the wrong thing to do. We shouldn't be adding new public functions unless we expect applications to actually call them.

Probably `util/mkerr.pl` needs to be updated so that it doesn't add these functions to public headers.
comments: I'd be happy to do so.  I need ideas on how to best register the new ones, so `util/mkerr.pl` doesn't suddenly start to remove old ones.
Either way, they should all be deprecated

> I'd be happy to do so. I need ideas on how to best register the new ones, so util/mkerr.pl doesn't suddenly start to remove old ones.

One possibility is to do it the same way that find-doc-nits knows when we introduce newly undocumented functions without complaining about old ones. We have a text file somewhere containing the list of ERR functions that should remain public.

> Either way, they should all be deprecated

Agreed.

review_comments: This file should be included from all the xxxerr.h files from libcrypto.
Yes, you're right.  I thought I had, but that may have gotten lost while I was juggling between this PR and #13392
Could the renaming of this define and other similar ones be considered an API break?
Why?  These headers were never installed anywhere...  and this is just a guard for this file.  At some point, they were called things like `HEADER_CAPI_ERR_H`, that got changed in 1.1.1 (!)
Why do we need this large number of internal header files - each of which looks virtually identical, and each of which declares one function. Can't we just collapse them all into a single header?

`util/mkerr.pl` can handle singular sub-libraries (also called "modules"), so from a processing point of view, it's simply easier that way.  I do have in mind that we might want to move more stuff into internal headers as time goes, and as long as we haven't turned around and made generation of error stuff monolithic, I believe we're stuck with this.  I don't plan to change that in this PR.
